title.zh: 卷一百三十七 列傳第二十四: 察罕 曲樞 阿禮海牙 奕赫抵雅爾丁 脫烈海牙
title.en: Volume 137 Biographies 24: Chahan, Qushu, Alihaiya, Yihediyaerding, Tuoliehaiya
title.raw: 卷一百三十七 列傳第二十四: 察罕 曲樞 阿禮海牙 奕赫抵雅爾丁 脫烈海牙 Volume 137 Biographies 24: Chahan, Qushu, Alihaiya, Yihediyaerding, Tuoliehaiya

sentences.zh: 察罕，西域板勒紇城人也。

translations.literal: Chahan was a native of Banlehe City in the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: Chahan came from Banlehe city in the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 父伯德那，歲庚辰，國兵下西域，舉族來歸。

translations.literal: His father Boridana—in the gengchen year, when the national army descended upon the Western Regions, the whole clan came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: His father Boridana: in a gengchen year, when the imperial armies reached the Western Regions, the entire clan submitted and settled.

sentences.zh: 事親王旭烈，授河東民賦副緫管，因居河中猗氏縣，後徙解州。

translations.literal: He served Prince Xulie, was appointed deputy commissioner-general of He'dong civilian taxation, and therefore dwelt in Yi County, Hezhong; later he moved to Xie Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served Prince Xulie and was made deputy commissioner for civilian levies in Hedong; the family settled at Yishi in Hezhong and later moved to Xiezhou.

sentences.zh: 贈榮祿大夫、宣徽使、柱國、芮國公。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Commissioner of the Palace Service, Pillar of the State, and Duke of Rui.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Palatial Intendant, Pillar of the State, and Duke of Rui.

sentences.zh: 察罕魁偉穎悟，博覽強記，通諸國字書，為行軍府奧魯千戶。

translations.literal: Chahan was tall and imposing, quick-witted, widely read with a powerful memory, versed in the scripts of many lands, and served as a thousand-household of the campaign headquarters' auru.
translations.idiomatic: Chahan was tall and brilliant, widely read and retentive, fluent in the scripts of many countries, and held the post of thousand-household in the campaign headquarters' auru.

sentences.zh: 奧魯赤參政湖廣，辟為蒙古都萬戶府知事。

translations.literal: When Aoluchi became administrative commissioner of Huguang, he recruited Chahan as secretary of the Mongol Chief Ten-Thousand Households Office.
translations.idiomatic: When Aoluchi became administrative commissioner of Huguang, he recruited Chahan as secretary of the Mongol Chief Ten-Thousand Households Office.

sentences.zh: 奧魯赤進平章，復辟為理問，政事悉委裁決，且令諸子受學焉。

translations.literal: When Aoluchi was promoted to Grand Councillor, he again recruited Chahan as judicial inquirer; all administrative matters were entrusted to his judgment, and he also had his sons study under him.
translations.idiomatic: When Aoluchi rose to Grand Councillor, he again appointed Chahan judicial inquirer, entrusted him with full authority over affairs, and had his sons study under him.

sentences.zh: 至元二十四年，從鎮南王征安南，師次瀘江。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Zhiyuan, he followed the Prince of Zhennan on the campaign against Annan; the army halted at the Lu River.
translations.idiomatic: In 1287 he followed the Prince of Zhennan against Annam; the army encamped on the Lu River.

sentences.zh: 安南世子遣其叔父詣軍門自陳無罪，王命察罕數其罪而責之，使者辭屈，世子舉衆逃去。

translations.literal: The crown prince of Annan sent his uncle to the army gate to declare his innocence; the prince ordered Chahan to enumerate his crimes and rebuke him. The envoy was reduced to silence, and the crown prince fled with his forces.
translations.idiomatic: The Annamese crown prince sent his uncle to the camp to plead innocence; the prince had Chahan list his crimes and rebuke him. When the envoy could not answer, the crown prince fled with his troops.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，授樞密院經歷。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, he was appointed secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1291 he was appointed secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 未幾從奧魯赤移治江西。

translations.literal: Before long he followed Aoluchi when his administration moved to Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he accompanied Aoluchi when his administration was transferred to Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 寧都民言：「某鄉石上雲氣五色，有物焉，視之玉璽也。

translations.literal: The people of Ningdu said, "On a stone in such-and-such village there are five-colored clouds; there is something there that, on inspection, is a jade seal.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Ningdu reported, "On a stone in a certain village there are five-colored clouds; what lies there looks like a jade imperial seal.

sentences.zh: 不以兵取，恐為居人所有。

translations.literal: If troops are not sent to take it, I fear the local residents will possess it."
translations.idiomatic: Unless troops are sent to seize it, the locals may claim it for themselves."

sentences.zh: 」衆惑之。

translations.literal: The multitude were bewildered by this.
translations.idiomatic: Many were taken in by the story.

sentences.zh: 察罕曰：「妄也，是必搆害仇家者。

translations.literal: Chahan said, "This is nonsense; it must be someone framing a rival clan."
translations.idiomatic: Chahan said, "This is nonsense—it must be someone framing a personal enemy."

sentences.zh: 」覈問之果然。

translations.literal: On rigorous inquiry it proved so.
translations.idiomatic: A thorough investigation proved him right.

sentences.zh: 前後從奧魯赤出入湖廣、江西兩省，凡二十一年，多著勳績。

translations.literal: In all, he followed Aoluchi in and out of the two provinces of Huguang and Jiangxi for twenty-one years, achieving many meritorious deeds.
translations.idiomatic: Over twenty-one years he served Aoluchi in Huguang and Jiangxi and won many distinctions.

sentences.zh: 成宗大德四年，御史臺奏僉湖南憲司事，中書省奏為武昌路治中。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Dade under Chengzong, the Censorate memorialized to appoint him concurrently to the Hunan surveillance commission; the Central Secretariat memorialized to make him assistant prefect of Wuchang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1300 the Censorate recommended him for concurrent service on the Hunan surveillance commission, while the Central Secretariat proposed him as assistant prefect of Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 丞相哈剌哈孫曰：「察罕廉潔，固宜居風憲。

translations.literal: The Chancellor Haraqasun said, "Chahan is incorrupt; he is indeed fit for surveillance duties.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Haraqasun said, "Chahan is incorrupt and well suited to surveillance work.

sentences.zh: 然武昌大郡，非斯人不可治。

translations.literal: Yet Wuchang is a great commandery; no one but this man can govern it."
translations.idiomatic: But Wuchang is a major prefecture—no one but he can govern it."

sentences.zh: 」竟除武昌。

translations.literal: In the end he was appointed to Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he was appointed to Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 廣西妖賊高仙道以左道惑衆，平民詿誤者以數千計。

translations.literal: The sorcerer-rebel Gao Xiandao of Guangxi deluded the masses with heterodox teachings; the common people misled numbered in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxi the sorcerer-rebel Gao Xiandao misled the people with heterodox teachings, and thousands of commoners were led astray.

sentences.zh: 既敗，湖廣行省命察罕與憲司雜治之，鞫得其情，議誅首惡數人，餘悉縱遣，且焚其籍。

translations.literal: After their defeat, the Huguang Branch Secretariat ordered Chahan and the surveillance commission to try the cases jointly; on examination the facts were obtained, and it was proposed to execute several ringleaders while releasing all the rest and burning their registers.
translations.idiomatic: After their defeat, the Huguang Branch Secretariat ordered Chahan and the surveillance officials to try the cases together. When the facts were established, they proposed executing a few ringleaders, releasing everyone else, and burning the registers.

sentences.zh: 衆難之。

translations.literal: The assembly objected.
translations.idiomatic: The others objected.

sentences.zh: 察罕曰：「吾獨當其責，諸君無累也。

translations.literal: Chahan said, "I alone shall bear the responsibility; you gentlemen need not be implicated."
translations.idiomatic: Chahan said, "I alone will bear the responsibility—you need not be implicated."

sentences.zh: 」以治最聞，擢河南省郎中。

translations.literal: For his governance he became known as foremost and was promoted to director of the Henan Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His administration won the highest praise, and he was promoted to director in the Henan Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 成宗崩，仁宗自藩邸入誅群臣之為異謀者，迎武宗于邊。

translations.literal: When Chengzong died, Renzong entered from his princely residence to execute the ministers who harbored divergent plots, and welcomed Wuzong from the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzong died, Renzong left his princely estate, executed ministers who had plotted treason, and went to the frontier to welcome Wuzong.

sentences.zh: 河南平章囊加台薦察罕，即驛召至上都，賜廄馬二匹、鈔一千貫、銀五十兩，曰：「卿少留，行用卿矣。

translations.literal: Nangatai, Grand Councillor of Henan, recommended Chahan; he was immediately summoned by post relay to Shangdu and granted two stable horses, a thousand strings of paper money, and fifty taels of silver, with the words, "Sir, stay a while—you will soon be employed."
translations.idiomatic: Nangatai, Grand Councillor of Henan, recommended Chahan, who was summoned at once by relay to Shangdu. He received two stable horses, a thousand strings of paper money, and fifty taels of silver, and was told, "Stay a little longer—you will soon be needed."

sentences.zh: 」武宗即位，立仁宗為皇太子，授察罕詹事院判，進僉詹事院事，賜銀百兩、錦二匹。

translations.literal: When Wuzong took the throne, he established Renzong as crown prince, appointed Chahan vice-director of the Household of the Heir Apparent, promoted him to concurrent director, and granted him a hundred taels of silver and two lengths of brocade.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzong ascended the throne he made Renzong crown prince, appointed Chahan vice-director of the Heir Apparent's household, then promoted him to concurrent director, and gave him a hundred taels of silver and two lengths of brocade.

sentences.zh: 遣先還大都立院事。

translations.literal: He was sent back first to Dadu to establish the household administration.
translations.idiomatic: Chahan was sent ahead to Dadu to set up the household administration.

sentences.zh: 仁宗至，謂曰：「上以故安西王地賜我，置都緫管府，卿其領之，慎揀僚屬，勿以詹事位高不屑此也。

translations.literal: When Renzong arrived, he said, "The emperor has granted me the former lands of the Prince of Anxi and established a chief commissionerate; you shall head it. Choose subordinates carefully, and do not disdain this post because your position as Household Director is lofty.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong arrived he said, "The emperor has granted me the former Anxi princely domain and set up a chief commissionerate—you shall head it. Choose your staff carefully, and do not look down on the post because your rank as Household Director is high.

sentences.zh: 進卿秩資德大夫。

translations.literal: I advance your rank to Grand Master of Supporting Virtue."
translations.idiomatic: I am raising your rank to Grand Master of Supporting Virtue."

sentences.zh: 」察罕叩頭謝曰：「都府之職，敢不恭命，進秩非所敢當。

translations.literal: Chahan kowtowed in thanks and said, "The post at the chief commissionerate—I dare not fail to obey; the promotion in rank is more than I dare accept."
translations.idiomatic: Chahan kowtowed and replied, "I dare not refuse the chief commissionerate, but the promotion is more than I deserve."

sentences.zh: 」固辭，改正奉大夫，授以銀印。

translations.literal: He firmly declined; his rank was changed to Grand Master for Proper Service, and he was granted a silver seal.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly declined; his rank was set at Grand Master for Proper Service, and he received a silver seal.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，拜中書參知政事，但緫持綱維，不屑細務，識者謂得大臣體。

translations.literal: When Renzong took the throne, Chahan was appointed Vice Director of the Central Secretariat; he only held the main lines of policy in hand and disdained petty matters—those who understood said he had grasped the bearing of a great minister.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong ascended the throne, Chahan was made Vice Director of the Central Secretariat. He held only the broad lines of policy and left petty affairs aside; observers said he had the bearing of a true statesman.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗賜枸杞酒，曰：「以益卿壽。

translations.literal: The emperor once bestowed wolfberry wine, saying, "To prolong your life."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once gave him wolfberry wine, saying, "To add years to your life."

sentences.zh: 」又語宰相曰：「察罕清素，可賜金束帶、鈔萬貫。

translations.literal: He also told the chancellors, "Chahan is pure and frugal; he may be granted a gold belt and ten thousand strings of paper money."
translations.idiomatic: He also told the chancellors, "Chahan lives plainly—give him a gold belt and ten thousand strings of paper money."

sentences.zh: 」前後賞賚不可勝計。

translations.literal: Rewards before and after were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards before and after were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 皇慶元年，進榮祿大夫、平章政事、商議中書省事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huangqing, he was advanced to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Grand Councillor, and Consultant on Central Secretariat Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1312 he was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Grand Councillor, and consultant on Central Secretariat affairs.

sentences.zh: 乞歸解州立碑先塋，許之。

translations.literal: He requested leave to return to Xie Prefecture to erect a stele at his ancestors' tombs; permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He asked leave to return to Xiezhou and set up a stele at his family's graves; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 暮年，居德安白雲山別墅，以白雲自號。

translations.literal: In his later years he dwelt at a villa on White Cloud Mountain in De'an and took White Cloud as his sobriquet.
translations.idiomatic: In old age he lived at a villa on White Cloud Mountain in De'an and styled himself Master White Cloud.

sentences.zh: 嘗入見，帝望見曰：「白雲先生來也。

translations.literal: Once when he came to audience, the emperor saw him from afar and said, "Master White Cloud has come."
translations.idiomatic: Once when he came to court, the emperor saw him from afar and said, "Master White Cloud has arrived."

sentences.zh: 」其被寵遇如此。

translations.literal: Such was the favor shown him.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the favor he enjoyed.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗問張良何如人，對曰：「佐高帝，興漢，功成身退，賢者也。

translations.literal: The emperor once asked what sort of man Zhang Liang was; he replied, "He assisted the High Emperor, raised Han, and when his work was done withdrew from office—a worthy man."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once asked what sort of man Zhang Liang was. Chahan replied, "He aided the founding emperor, helped raise Han, and withdrew once his work was done—a true worthy."

sentences.zh: 」又問狄仁傑，對曰：「當唐室中衰，能卒保社稷，亦賢相也。

translations.literal: He was asked about Di Renjie and replied, "When the Tang house was in mid-decline, he was able in the end to preserve the altars of state—he too was a worthy chancellor."
translations.idiomatic: Asked about Di Renjie, he said, "When the Tang was in decline he still preserved the realm in the end—another worthy chancellor."

sentences.zh: 」因誦范仲淹所撰碑詞甚熟。

translations.literal: Thereupon he recited from memory the stele text composed by Fan Zhongyan with great fluency.
translations.idiomatic: He then recited from memory the stele inscription Fan Zhongyan had written, word for word.

sentences.zh: 帝歎息良久曰：「察罕博學如此邪。

translations.literal: The emperor sighed long and said, "Chahan is so learned as this!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed and said, "Chahan is this learned!"

sentences.zh: 」嘗譯貞觀政要以獻。

translations.literal: He once translated the Essentials of Government in the Zhenguan Reign and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: He once translated the Essentials of Government from the Zhenguan era and presented it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，詔繕寫遍賜左右。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and ordered it copied and distributed widely to those at his side.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and ordered copies made for all his close attendants.

sentences.zh: 且詔譯帝範。

translations.literal: He also ordered a translation of the Models of the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered a translation of the Models of the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 又命譯脫必赤顏名曰聖武開天紀，及紀年纂要、太宗平金始末等書，俱付史館。

translations.literal: He further ordered translated the Tuobichiyan work entitled Record of the Sacred Martial Opening of Heaven, as well as Essentials of Chronology, the Complete Account of Taizong's Pacification of Jin, and other books—all delivered to the Historiography Office.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered translated the Tuobichiyan work called Record of the Sacred Martial Opening of Heaven, along with Essentials of Chronology, the Complete Account of Taizong's Pacification of Jin, and other works, all of which were sent to the Historiography Office.

sentences.zh: 嘗以病請告，暨還朝，帝御萬歲山圓殿，與平章李孟入謝。

translations.literal: Once he requested leave on grounds of illness; when he returned to court, the emperor held audience in the round hall on Longevity Mountain, and he entered with Grand Councillor Li Meng to give thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Once he took sick leave; when he returned to court the emperor received him in the round hall on Longevity Mountain, and he entered with Grand Councillor Li Meng to give thanks.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「白雲病愈邪？

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Has Master White Cloud recovered from his illness?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Has Master White Cloud recovered?"

sentences.zh: 」頓首對曰：「老臣衰病，無補聖明，荷陛下哀矜，放歸田里，幸甚，不覺沉痾去體爾。

translations.literal: He kowtowed and replied, "This old minister's declining illness is of no help to your sagely clarity; I am indebted to Your Majesty's compassion in releasing me to the countryside—greatly fortunate; I did not notice my grave malady leave my body."
translations.idiomatic: He kowtowed and said, "This old servant's weakness is of no use to your wisdom. Thanks to your compassion in letting me return home, I am most fortunate—my grave illness has left me without my noticing."

sentences.zh: 」命賜茵以坐。

translations.literal: He was ordered granted a cushion and seated.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had a cushion brought for him to sit on.

sentences.zh: 顧李孟曰：「知止不辱，今見其人。

translations.literal: Turning to Li Meng, he said, "To know when to stop and avoid disgrace—today I see such a man."
translations.idiomatic: Turning to Li Meng he said, "Knowing when to stop and keep one's honor—today I see such a man."

sentences.zh: 朕始以荅剌罕、不憐吉台、囊加台等言用之，誠多裨益。

translations.literal: At first I employed him on the word of Darqan, Bulinjutai, Nangatai, and others—he has truly been of much benefit.
translations.idiomatic: I first employed him on the recommendation of Darqan, Bulinjutai, Nangatai, and others, and he has truly been of great help.

sentences.zh: 有言察罕不善者，其人即非善人也。

translations.literal: Whoever speaks ill of Chahan is himself not a good man.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever speaks ill of Chahan is not a good man himself.

sentences.zh: 」又語及科舉并前古帝王賜姓命氏之事，因賜察罕姓白氏。

translations.literal: He also spoke of the civil examinations and of how ancient emperors granted surnames and established clans, and thereupon granted Chahan the surname Bai.
translations.idiomatic: He also spoke of the civil examinations and of how ancient emperors granted surnames and clans, and bestowed on Chahan the surname Bai.

sentences.zh: 初，察罕生於河中，其夜，天氣清肅，月白如晝。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Chahan was born in Hezhong, that night the weather was clear and still, and the moon was white as daylight.
translations.idiomatic: When Chahan was born in Hezhong, the night was clear and still, and the moon shone white as day.

sentences.zh: 相者賀曰：「是兒必貴。

translations.literal: A physiognomist congratulated them, saying, "This child will surely be noble."
translations.idiomatic: A physiognomist congratulated the family, saying, "This boy will surely rise high."

sentences.zh: 」國人謂白為察罕，故名察罕。

translations.literal: The people of the realm called white chahan, and so he was named Chahan.
translations.idiomatic: In the realm white was called chahan, and so he was given the name Chahan.

sentences.zh: 察罕天性孝友，田宅之在河中者，悉分與諸昆弟。

translations.literal: Chahan was filial and brotherly by nature; all fields and houses he had in Hezhong he divided among his brothers.
translations.idiomatic: By nature Chahan was filial and brotherly; he divided all his land and houses in Hezhong among his brothers.

sentences.zh: 昆弟貧來歸者，復分與田宅奴婢，縱奴為民者甚衆。

translations.literal: When brothers returned in poverty, he again divided fields, houses, and slaves among them; the slaves he freed to become commoners were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: When poor brothers came to him, he again gave them land, houses, and servants, and freed many slaves to become commoners.

sentences.zh: 故人多稱長者。

translations.literal: Therefore many called him a man of virtue.
translations.idiomatic: For this many called him a man of true generosity.

sentences.zh: 既致仕，優游八年，以壽終。

translations.literal: After he retired from office, he lived at ease for eight years and died at a full age.
translations.idiomatic: After retirement he lived at ease for eight years and died at a full age.

sentences.zh: 子外家奴，太中大夫、武岡路緫管；

translations.literal: His son Waijianu—Grand Master of the Palace, circuit intendant of Wugang;
translations.idiomatic: His son Waijianu was Grand Master of the Palace and circuit intendant of Wugang;

sentences.zh: 李家奴，早卒；

translations.literal: Lijianu, who died young;
translations.idiomatic: Lijianu, who died young;

sentences.zh: 忽都篤，承直郎、高郵府判官。

translations.literal: Hutudu, Gentleman for Supporting Uprightness, assistant prefect of Gaoyou.
translations.idiomatic: and Hutudu, Gentleman for Supporting Uprightness and assistant prefect of Gaoyou.

sentences.zh: 孫九人，仕者二人：闊闊不花、哈撒。

translations.literal: He had nine grandsons; two entered office: Kuokuobuhua and Hasa.
translations.idiomatic: He had nine grandsons; two held office: Kuokuobuhua and Hasa.

sentences.zh: 曲樞，西土人。

translations.literal: Qushu was a man of the western lands.
translations.idiomatic: Qushu was a native of the western regions.

sentences.zh: 曾祖達不台，祖阿達台，父質理花台，世贈功臣，追封王爵。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather was Dabutai, his grandfather Adatai, his father Zhilihuatai; generation after generation they were posthumously granted the title of meritorious minister and ennobled with princely rank.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather was Dabutai, his grandfather Adatai, and his father Zhilihuatai; for generations the family received posthumous honors as meritorious ministers and princely titles.

sentences.zh: 曲樞七歲失怙恃。

translations.literal: Qushu lost both parents at the age of seven.
translations.idiomatic: Qushu lost both parents when he was seven.

sentences.zh: 既壯，沉密靜專，為徽仁裕聖皇太后宮臣。

translations.literal: When grown, he was deep, reserved, quiet, and single-minded, and became a palace attendant of the Empress Dowager of Sagely Benevolence and Abundant Grace.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age he was grave, discreet, and steady, and became an attendant in the palace of the Empress Dowager of Sagely Benevolence and Abundant Grace.

sentences.zh: 仁宗幼時，以曲樞可任保傅，左右擁翼。

translations.literal: When Renzong was young, because Qushu was fit to serve as guardian and tutor, he was kept at his side to support and protect him.
translations.idiomatic: In Renzong's youth Qushu was judged fit to be his guardian and tutor and was kept at his side to support and protect him.

sentences.zh: 曲樞入則佐視食飲，出則抱負游衍，鞠躬盡力，夙夜匪懈。

translations.literal: Qushu within assisted in overseeing food and drink; without he carried and bore him on outings—bowing with full effort, diligent morning and night without slackening.
translations.idiomatic: Within the palace Qushu helped watch over his meals; outside he carried him on outings. He bent every effort to the task and never slackened, day or night.

sentences.zh: 大德三年，武宗緫戎北邊。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dade, Wuzong commanded the armies on the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In 1299 Wuzong took command of the northern armies.

sentences.zh: 九年，讒人亂國。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, slanderers threw the state into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: In 1305 slanderers threw the court into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 仁宗侍皇太后之國于懷，未幾，復之雲中，連年奔走不暇。

translations.literal: Renzong attended the empress dowager when she went to live in Huai; before long they returned to Yunzhong, and for years they were on the move without rest.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong accompanied the empress dowager when she withdrew to Huai; soon they were back in Yunzhong, and for years they were constantly on the move.

sentences.zh: 曲樞櫛風沐雨，跋涉艱險，無倦色。

translations.literal: Qushu braved wind and rain, traversed hardships and dangers, and showed no sign of weariness.
translations.idiomatic: Qushu braved wind and rain and hard roads without ever showing weariness.

sentences.zh: 成宗崩，仁宗奉太后入朝，殲姦黨，迎武宗即皇帝位，仁宗為皇太子，天下以安。

translations.literal: When Chengzong died, Renzong escorted the empress dowager to court, destroyed the faction of traitors, welcomed Wuzong to the imperial throne, and made Renzong crown prince—the realm was thereby settled.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzong died, Renzong brought the empress dowager to court, destroyed the traitorous faction, and welcomed Wuzong to the throne; Renzong was made crown prince and the realm was at peace.

sentences.zh: 拜曲樞榮祿大夫、平章政事，行大司農。

translations.literal: Qushu was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Grand Councillor, acting as chief minister of agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: Qushu was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Grand Councillor, with concurrent charge of the chief ministry of agriculture.

sentences.zh: 未幾，進光祿大夫，領詹事院事，加特進，封應國公。

translations.literal: Before long he was advanced to Grand Master of the Palace, took charge of the Household of the Heir Apparent, was given the special advancement, and enfeoffed as Duke of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to Grand Master of the Palace, put in charge of the Heir Apparent's household, granted special advancement, and enfeoffed as Duke of Ying.

sentences.zh: 至大元年，拜開府儀同三司、太子詹事、平章軍國重事、上柱國，依前大司農、應國公。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhida, he was appointed Grand Preceptor with the same ceremonial as the Three Excellencies, Household Director of the Heir Apparent, Grand Councillor for Military and State Affairs of the First Rank, and Pillar of the State, while retaining his former posts as chief minister of agriculture and Duke of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: In 1308 he was made Grand Preceptor with ceremonial equal to the Three Excellencies, Household Director of the Heir Apparent, Grand Councillor for Military and State Affairs of the First Rank, and Pillar of the State, while retaining his posts as chief minister of agriculture and Duke of Ying.

sentences.zh: 進太子太保，領典醫監事。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and took charge of the Directorate of Imperial Physicians.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and put in charge of the Directorate of Imperial Physicians.

sentences.zh: 四年，授太保、錄軍國重事、集賢大學士，兼大司農，領崇祥院、司天臺事，官爵勳封如故。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was appointed Grand Mentor, Recorder of Military and State Affairs of the First Rank, and Grand Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, while concurrently serving as chief minister of agriculture and taking charge of the Chongxiang Court and the Directorate of Astronomy; his offices, titles, merit, and enfeoffment remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In 1311 he was made Grand Mentor, Recorder of Military and State Affairs of the First Rank, and Grand Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, while retaining the chief ministry of agriculture and taking charge of the Chongxiang Court and the Directorate of Astronomy; his other titles and honors were unchanged.

sentences.zh: 後以疾薨于位。

translations.literal: Later he died in office of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He later died in office of illness.

sentences.zh: 子二人。

translations.literal: He had two sons.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons.

sentences.zh: 長伯都，大德十一年特授翰林學士、嘉議大夫，遷中奉大夫、典寶監卿，加資德大夫、治書侍御史。

translations.literal: The elder, Bodu—in the eleventh year of Dade was specially appointed Hanlin Academician and Grand Master of Court Discussion, then transferred to Grand Master for Supporting Service and Director of the Directorate of Imperial Treasures, and advanced to Grand Master of Supporting Virtue and Attending Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: The elder son Bodu: in 1307 he was specially made Hanlin Academician and Grand Master of Court Discussion, then promoted to Grand Master for Supporting Service and Director of the Directorate of Imperial Treasures, and later to Grand Master of Supporting Virtue and Attending Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 至大元年，陞榮祿大夫，遙授中書平章政事，改侍御史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhida, he was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, appointed in absentia as Grand Councillor of the Central Secretariat, and transferred to Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1308 he was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, given the honorary title of Grand Councillor of the Central Secretariat, and made Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 明年，拜中書參知政事，進右丞，年三十二而卒。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed Vice Director of the Central Secretariat, advanced to Right Chancellor, and died at the age of thirty-two.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made Vice Director of the Central Secretariat and promoted to Right Chancellor; he died at thirty-two.

sentences.zh: 子咬住。

translations.literal: His son was Yaozhu.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Yaozhu.

sentences.zh: 阿禮海牙

translations.literal: Alihaiya
translations.idiomatic: Alihaiya

sentences.zh: 阿禮海牙，畏吾氏，集賢大學士脫列之子也。

translations.literal: Alihaiya was of the Uyghur clan; he was the son of Tuolie, Grand Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Alihaiya was a Uyghur and the son of Tuolie, Grand Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 兄野訥，事仁宗於潛邸。

translations.literal: His elder brother Yene served Renzong at his hidden residence.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Yene had served Renzong when he was still in his princely household.

sentences.zh: 大德九年，仁宗奉興聖太后出居懷州。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Dade, Renzong escorted the Empress Dowager of Sagely Birth out to reside in Huai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 1305 Renzong accompanied the Empress Dowager of Sagely Birth when she withdrew to Huai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 從者單弱，多懷去計。

translations.literal: The followers were few and weak; many harbored plans to leave.
translations.idiomatic: The entourage was small and weak, and many thought of leaving.

sentences.zh: 野訥獨無所畏難。

translations.literal: Yene alone showed no fear or difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: Yene alone showed no fear or hesitation.

sentences.zh: 成宗崩，權臣阿附中宮，不遣使告哀宗藩。

translations.literal: When Chengzong died, the powerful minister Azhong controlled the inner palace and did not send envoys to announce the mourning to the princely domains.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzong died, the powerful minister Azhong controlled the inner palace and sent no envoys to announce the mourning to the princes.

sentences.zh: 仁宗有聞，將自懷州入京，宮臣或持不可。

translations.literal: Renzong heard of it and was about to enter the capital from Huai Prefecture; some palace attendants held that this should not be done.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong heard of it he prepared to enter the capital from Huai Prefecture, but some palace attendants argued against it.

sentences.zh: 野訥屏人密啟曰：「天子晏駕而皇子已早卒，天下無主，邪謀方興。

translations.literal: Yene dismissed attendants and secretly reported, saying, "The Son of Heaven has passed away and the crown prince died young; the realm has no ruler, and treacherous plots are rising.
translations.idiomatic: Yene sent everyone away and secretly urged, "The emperor is dead and the crown prince died young. The realm has no master, and treacherous plots are rising.

sentences.zh: 懷寧王及殿下，世祖、裕皇賢孫，人心所屬久矣。

translations.literal: The Prince of Huaining and Your Highness are worthy grandsons of Shizu and Yuzong; the hearts of the people have long been with you.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Huaining and Your Highness are worthy grandsons of Shizu and Yuzong, and the people's hearts have long been with you.

sentences.zh: 宜急奉太母入定大計，邪謀必止。

translations.literal: You should urgently escort the Grand Empress Dowager to settle the great plan—the treacherous plots will surely cease.
translations.idiomatic: You should hurry to bring the Grand Empress Dowager in and settle the succession—the plots will collapse.

sentences.zh: 迎立懷寧王以正神器，在此行矣。

translations.literal: To welcome and establish the Prince of Huaining to rectify the imperial regalia—this depends on this journey."
translations.idiomatic: Welcoming the Prince of Huaining to the throne and securing the regalia depends on this move alone."

sentences.zh: 」仁宗即白太后，以二月至京師，遂誅柄臣二人，遣使迎武宗。

translations.literal: Renzong immediately informed the empress dowager; in the second month they reached the capital, executed two powerful ministers, and sent envoys to welcome Wuzong.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong at once told the empress dowager; in the second month they reached the capital, executed two powerful ministers, and sent envoys to welcome Wuzong.

sentences.zh: 武宗即位，召野訥，賜玉帶，授嘉議大夫、祕書監。

translations.literal: When Wuzong took the throne, he summoned Yene, granted him a jade belt, and appointed him Grand Master of Court Discussion and Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzong ascended the throne he summoned Yene, gave him a jade belt, and appointed him Grand Master of Court Discussion and Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 仁宗居東宮，兼太子右庶子，遷侍御史、崇祥院使，兼將作院使。

translations.literal: When Renzong resided in the Eastern Palace, Yene concurrently served as Right Mentor of the Heir Apparent, then was transferred to Attending Censor, Director of the Chongxiang Court, and concurrently Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings.
translations.idiomatic: While Renzong was crown prince, Yene also served as Right Mentor of the Heir Apparent, then became Attending Censor, Director of the Chongxiang Court, and concurrently Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings.

sentences.zh: 閩有綉工，工官大集民間子女居肆督責，吏因為奸利，野訥奏罷之，閩人感悅。

translations.literal: In Min there were embroidery workers; the craft officials gathered many commoners' sons and daughters into shops to supervise and compel them, and clerks profited corruptly thereby. Yene memorialized to abolish this, and the people of Min were grateful and pleased.
translations.idiomatic: In Fujian, craft officials herded commoners' children into workshops to drive embroidery labor while clerks profited corruptly. Yene memorialized to end the practice, and the people of Min were grateful.

sentences.zh: 尋兼太醫院使。

translations.literal: Soon he was concurrently made Director of the Imperial Medical Service.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was also made Director of the Imperial Medical Service.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，請召文武老臣，咨以朝政。

translations.literal: When Renzong took the throne, Yene requested that veteran civil and military officials be summoned to consult on court affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong ascended the throne, Yene asked that veteran civil and military officials be summoned to advise on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 又請以中都苑囿還諸民。

translations.literal: He also requested that the parks and preserves of the central capital be returned to the people.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that the imperial parks around the central capital be returned to the people.

sentences.zh: 拜樞密院副使，進同知樞密院事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and advanced to Concurrent Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and promoted to Concurrent Director.

sentences.zh: 命為中書平章政事，辭不拜。

translations.literal: He was ordered to serve as Grand Councillor of the Central Secretariat but declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was offered the post of Grand Councillor of the Central Secretariat but declined.

sentences.zh: 野訥之在臺及侍禁中，於國家事有不便，輒言之，言無不納。

translations.literal: While Yene was at the Censorate and attending within the forbidden precincts, whenever state affairs were disadvantageous he spoke of them, and his words were never rejected.
translations.idiomatic: Whether at the Censorate or in attendance within the palace, whenever he saw something harmful to the state he spoke up, and his advice was always accepted.

sentences.zh: 然韜晦惡盈，不泄於外。

translations.literal: Yet he concealed himself and hated excess, not letting matters leak outward.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he kept a low profile and hated excess, and never let grievances spill outside.

sentences.zh: 延祐四年卒，年四十。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yanyou he died at the age of forty.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1317 at the age of forty.

sentences.zh: 贈推誠保節翊運功臣、金紫光祿大夫、行中書省左丞相、上柱國、趙國公，諡忠靖。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted the title of Meritorious Minister Who Supports Sincerity, Preserves Integrity, and Aids the Dynasty, Grand Master of the Golden Purple and Golden Seal, Acting Left Chancellor of the Central Secretariat, Pillar of the State, and Duke of Zhao, with the posthumous name Zhongjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Meritorious Minister Who Supports Sincerity, Preserves Integrity, and Aids the Dynasty, Grand Master of the Golden Purple and Golden Seal, Acting Left Chancellor of the Central Secretariat, Pillar of the State, and Duke of Zhao, with the posthumous name Loyal and Tranquil.

sentences.zh: 阿禮海牙亦早事武宗、仁宗，為宿衛，以清慎通敏與父兄並見信任。

translations.literal: Alihaiya also early served Wuzong and Renzong as a palace guard; for his purity, caution, penetration, and quickness he was trusted together with his father and elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Alihaiya had also served Wuzong and Renzong early on as a palace guard; for his integrity, caution, and sharp intelligence he was trusted along with his father and brother.

sentences.zh: 十餘年間，歷華近，入侍帷幄，出踐省闥，廷無間言。

translations.literal: Over more than ten years he rose through lofty and intimate posts—within he attended the imperial curtains, without he trod the provincial gates—and at court there was no dissenting word.
translations.idiomatic: For more than ten years he rose through the highest posts—serving within the imperial curtains and governing in the provinces—and at court no one spoke against him.

sentences.zh: 至治初，出為平章政事，歷鎮江浙、湖廣、河南、陝西四省，皆有惠政，汴人尤懷思之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhizhi he went out as Grand Councillor, successively governing the four provinces of Jiang-Zhe, Huguang, Henan, and Shaanxi; in each he had benevolent policies, and the people of Bian especially cherished his memory.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Zhizhi reign he was sent out as Grand Councillor and governed Jiang-Zhe, Huguang, Henan, and Shaanxi in turn; everywhere his rule brought benefit, and the people of Bian cherished him most of all.

sentences.zh: 歸朝拜翰林學士承旨。

translations.literal: On returning to court he was appointed Chief Academician of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court he was made Chief Academician of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，解官家居。

translations.literal: Upon his father's death he left office and lived at home.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he left office and lived at home in mourning.

sentences.zh: 天曆元年秋，文宗入承大統。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the first year of Tianli, Wenzong entered to receive the great succession.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of 1328 Wenzong succeeded to the throne.

sentences.zh: 阿禮海牙即易服南迎，至於汴郊見焉。

translations.literal: Alihaiya immediately changed his dress and went south to welcome him, meeting him at the outskirts of Bian.
translations.idiomatic: Alihaiya at once changed his dress and went south to welcome him, meeting him on the outskirts of Bian.

sentences.zh: 帝命復鎮汴省。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered him to resume governing the Bian Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered him back to govern the Henan Branch Secretariat at Bian.

sentences.zh: 時當艱難之際，阿禮海牙高價糴粟，以峙糧儲，命近郡分治戎器，閱士卒，括馬民間，以備不虞。

translations.literal: At a time of hardship, Alihaiya bought grain at high prices to stock reserves, ordered nearby commanderies to prepare weapons separately, reviewed soldiers, and requisitioned horses among the people against the unforeseen.
translations.idiomatic: In those hard times Alihaiya bought grain at high prices to build reserves, ordered nearby prefectures to ready weapons, inspected troops, and requisitioned horses from the populace against emergencies.

sentences.zh: 先是，文宗即位之詔已播告天下，而陝西官府結連靖安王等起兵，東擊潼關。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wenzong's accession edict had already been proclaimed throughout the realm, yet the officials of Shaanxi joined with the Prince of Jing'an and others to raise troops and strike east at Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong's accession edict had already been proclaimed, yet officials in Shaanxi joined the Prince of Jing'an and others in rebellion and marched east against Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 阿禮海牙開府庫，量出鈔二十五萬緡，屬諸行省參政河南淮北蒙古軍都萬戶朶列圖、廉訪副使萬家閭犒軍河南以禦之。

translations.literal: Alihaiya opened the treasury and measured out two hundred fifty thousand strings of paper money, entrusting Duolietu, Branch Secretariat administrative commissioner and Chief Ten-Thousand Household of the Henan and Huaibei Mongol Army, and Wanjialu, vice surveillance commissioner, to reward the army in Henan to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: Alihaiya opened the treasury and issued two hundred fifty thousand strings of paper money, charging Duolietu, administrative commissioner of the branch secretariat and chief ten-thousand household of the Henan and Huaibei Mongol army, and Wanjialu, vice surveillance commissioner, to reward troops in Henan for the defense.

sentences.zh: 令都鎮撫卜伯率軍吏巡行南陽、高門、武關、荊子諸隘，南至襄、川二江之口，督以嚴備。

translations.literal: He ordered the metropolitan pacification commissioner Bobo to lead military officers on patrol through the passes of Nanyang, Gaomen, Wuguan, and Jingzi, south to the mouths of the Xiang and Chuan rivers, urging strict preparedness.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Metropolitan Pacification Commissioner Bobo to patrol the passes at Nanyang, Gaomen, Wuguan, and Jingzi, south to the mouths of the Xiang and Chuan rivers, and enforce strict readiness.

sentences.zh: 萬戶博羅守潼關，不能軍。

translations.literal: The ten-thousand household Boluo guarded Tong Pass but could not hold the army in order.
translations.idiomatic: The ten-thousand household Boluo held Tong Pass but could not keep his troops in order.

sentences.zh: 是月二十五日，只兒哈率小汪緫帥、脫帖木兒萬戶等之兵，突出潼關，東掠閿鄉，披靈寶，盪陝州、新安諸郡邑，放兵四劫，迤邐前進。

translations.literal: On the twenty-fifth day of that month, Zhi'erha led the troops of the commander-in-chief Xiaowang, the ten-thousand household Tuotiemuer, and others in a sudden breakout from Tong Pass, raiding east through Minxiang, sweeping Lingbao, and overrunning the prefectures and counties of Shaanzhou, Xin'an, and others; they let their soldiers plunder on all sides and advanced in succession.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-fifth of that month Zhi'erha led the forces of Commander-in-Chief Xiaowang, Ten-Thousand Household Tuotiemuer, and others in a sudden breakout from Tong Pass. They raided east through Minxiang and Lingbao, overran Shaanzhou, Xin'an, and neighboring counties, let their troops plunder everywhere, and pressed forward.

sentences.zh: 河南告急之使狎至，而朶列圖亦以兵寡為言。

translations.literal: Messengers from Henan reporting urgent danger arrived in quick succession, and Duolietu also spoke of having too few troops.
translations.idiomatic: Urgent dispatches from Henan arrived one after another, and Duolietu too reported that his forces were too few.

sentences.zh: 十月一日，阿禮海牙集省憲官屬，問以長策，無有言者。

translations.literal: On the first day of the tenth month, Alihaiya assembled the officials of the secretariat and surveillance commission and asked for a long-term plan; no one spoke.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the tenth month Alihaiya assembled secretariat and surveillance officials and asked for a plan; no one had an answer.

sentences.zh: 阿禮海牙曰：「汴在南北之交，使西人得至此，則江南三省之道不通于畿甸，軍旅應接何日息乎。

translations.literal: Alihaiya said, "Bian lies at the junction of north and south. If the western forces reach here, the routes of the three southern provinces will not reach the capital region—when will military responses ever cease?"
translations.idiomatic: Alihaiya said, "Bian stands at the crossroads of north and south. If the western rebels reach here, the three southern provinces will be cut off from the capital—when would the fighting ever end?"

sentences.zh: 夫事有緩急輕重，今重莫如足兵，急莫如足食。

translations.literal: Matters have degrees of urgency and weight; now nothing is weightier than sufficient troops, nothing more urgent than sufficient food.
translations.idiomatic: Every crisis has its priorities: nothing matters more now than enough troops, nothing is more urgent than enough grain.

sentences.zh: 吾徵湖廣之平陽、保定兩翼軍，與吾省之鄧新翼、廬州、沂、郯砲弩手諸軍，以備虎牢；

translations.literal: I shall summon the Pingyang and Baoding wing armies of Huguang, together with the Dengxin wing, Luzhou, Yi, and Tan catapult-and-crossbow corps of our province, to defend Hulao;
translations.idiomatic: I will summon the Pingyang and Baoding wing armies from Huguang, together with our province's Dengxin wing, Luzhou, Yi, and Tan catapult and crossbow units, to hold Hulao;

sentences.zh: 裕州哈剌魯、鄧州孫萬戶兩軍，以備武關、荊子口。

translations.literal: the Halalu army of Yuzhou and the ten-thousand household Sun's army of Dengzhou, to defend Wuguan and Jingzikou.
translations.idiomatic: the Halalu army of Yuzhou and Ten-Thousand Household Sun's army of Dengzhou to guard Wuguan and Jingzikou.

sentences.zh: 以屬郡之兵及蒙古兩都萬戶、左右兩衛、諸部丁壯之可入軍者，給馬乘貲裝，立行伍，以次備諸隘。

translations.literal: With the troops of subordinate commanderies and the two metropolitan ten-thousand households of the Mongols, the left and right guards, and able-bodied men of the various divisions fit for service—I shall provide horses, travel funds, and equipment, form ranks, and in order man all the passes.
translations.idiomatic: With troops from subordinate prefectures, the two metropolitan Mongol ten-thousand households, the left and right guards, and every able-bodied man who can serve, I will supply horses, funds, and gear, form ranks, and man the passes in turn.

sentences.zh: 芍陂等屯兵本自襄、鄧諸軍來田者，還其軍，益以民之丁壯，使守襄陽、白土、峽州諸隘。

translations.literal: The garrison soldiers at Shaopi and elsewhere originally came from the Xiang and Deng armies to farm the fields; return them to their armies and supplement them with civilian able-bodied men to guard the passes at Xiangyang, Baitu, and Xiazhou.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison farmers at Shaopi and elsewhere originally came from the Xiang and Deng armies; send them back to their units and add civilian recruits to hold Xiangyang, Baitu, and Xiazhou.

sentences.zh: 別遣塔海以備自蜀至者，以汴、汝、荊、襄、兩淮之馬以給之，府庫不足，則命郡縣假諸殷富之家。

translations.literal: Send Tahai separately to guard against forces coming from Shu; supply him with horses from Bian, Ru, Jing, Xiang, and the two Huai circuits, and if the treasury is insufficient, order commanderies and counties to borrow from wealthy households.
translations.idiomatic: Send Tahai separately to block any advance from Shu, supply him with horses from Bian, Ru, Jing, Xiang, and the two Huai regions, and if the treasury falls short, have prefectures and counties borrow from wealthy families.

sentences.zh: 安豐等郡之粟，溯黃河運至于陝，糴諸汴、汝，近郡者，則運諸滎陽以達於虎牢。

translations.literal: Grain from Anfeng and other commanderies shall be transported up the Yellow River to Shaan; buy grain at Bian and Ru, and from nearby commanderies transport it to Xingyang to reach Hulao.
translations.idiomatic: Ship grain from Anfeng and other prefectures up the Yellow River toward Shaan; buy grain at Bian and Ru, and from nearby prefectures move it to Xingyang and on to Hulao.

sentences.zh: 吾與諸軍各奮忠義以從王事，宜無不濟者。

translations.literal: If I and the various armies each exert loyalty and righteousness in the royal service, there should be nothing we cannot achieve."
translations.idiomatic: If we and every army give our loyal best to the throne's cause, we should succeed."

sentences.zh: 」衆曰：「唯。

translations.literal: The assembly said, "Yes."
translations.idiomatic: Everyone answered, "Yes."

sentences.zh: 」命即日部分行事。

translations.literal: He ordered arrangements to be made and carried out that very day.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the plan put into action that same day.

sentences.zh: 自伯顏不花王以下省都事李元德等，凡省之屬吏與有官而家居者，各授以事而出。

translations.literal: From Prince Bayanbuhua down to the secretariat director Yuan Yuande and others, all subordinate clerks of the secretariat and officials living at home were each assigned duties and sent out.
translations.idiomatic: From Prince Bayanbuhua down to Secretariat Director Li Yuande and the rest, every clerk and official at home on leave was given a task and sent out.

sentences.zh: 廉訪使董守中、僉事沙沙在南陽，右丞脫帖木兒、廉訪使卜顏在虎牢，分遣兵馬以聽其調用。

translations.literal: Surveillance commissioner Dong Shouzhong and administrative aide Shasha were at Nanyang; right chancellor Tuotiemuer and surveillance commissioner Buyan were at Hulao; troops were dispatched separately to obey their orders.
translations.idiomatic: Surveillance Commissioner Dong Shouzhong and Administrative Aide Shasha were at Nanyang; Right Chancellor Tuotiemuer and Surveillance Commissioner Buyan at Hulao; troops were sent to each to follow their orders.

sentences.zh: 餽餉之行，千車相望，阿禮海牙親閱實之，必豐必良，信以期會。

translations.literal: Supply convoys went forth, a thousand carts in sight of one another; Alihaiya personally inspected and verified them—they must be ample and good, and reliable as to schedule.
translations.idiomatic: Supply trains rolled out by the thousand; Alihaiya personally inspected every load to ensure it was ample, sound, and on time.

sentences.zh: 自虎牢之南至於襄、漢，無不畢給。

translations.literal: From south of Hulao to Xiang and Han, nothing was left unsupplied.
translations.idiomatic: From south of Hulao to the Xiang and Han regions, nothing was left unsupplied.

sentences.zh: 蓋為粟二十萬石，豆如之，兵甲五十五萬，芻萬萬。

translations.literal: In all there were two hundred thousand piculs of grain, beans in like amount, five hundred fifty thousand sets of arms and armor, and ten thousand ten-thousands of fodder.
translations.idiomatic: In all they gathered two hundred thousand piculs of grain, as many of beans, five hundred fifty thousand sets of arms and armor, and a vast quantity of fodder.

sentences.zh: 是時，朝廷置行樞密院以緫西事。

translations.literal: At this time the court established a mobile Bureau of Military Affairs to oversee western affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the court set up a mobile Bureau of Military Affairs to direct the western campaign.

sentences.zh: 襄、漢、荊湖、河南郡縣皆缺官，阿禮海牙便宜擇材以處之，朝廷皆從其請。

translations.literal: In the Xiang, Han, Jinghu, and Henan commanderies and counties offices were all vacant; Alihaiya provisionally selected talent to fill them, and the court approved all his requests.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures and counties across Xiang, Han, Jinghu, and Henan lacked officials; Alihaiya appointed capable men on his own authority, and the court approved every request.

sentences.zh: 是月，西兵逼河南，行院使來報，曰：「西人北行者度河中以趨懷、孟、磁；

translations.literal: That month, as western troops pressed Henan, the mobile bureau commissioner came with a report, saying, "Those westerners going north cross the Yellow River to advance on Huai, Meng, and Ci;
translations.idiomatic: That month, as western troops pressed Henan, the mobile bureau commissioner reported, "The northern column is crossing the Yellow River toward Huai, Meng, and Ci;

sentences.zh: 南行者帖木哥，過武關，掠鄧州而殘之，直趨襄陽，攻破郡邑三十餘，橫絕數千里，所過殺官吏，焚廬舍，虜民人婦女財物，賊虐殄盡，西結囊家469f以蜀兵至矣。

translations.literal: those going south, Temuge, passed Wuguan, ravaged Dengzhou and laid it waste, pressed straight on Xiangyang, stormed more than thirty prefectures and counties, cut off thousands of li, and wherever they passed killed officials, burned dwellings, seized the people, women, and goods—plundering to extinction; in the west they joined with Niejiasai and Shu troops were arriving."
translations.idiomatic: the southern column under Temuge has passed Wuguan, ravaged Dengzhou, and driven straight on Xiangyang, taking more than thirty prefectures and counties and laying waste for thousands of li—killing officials, burning homes, and seizing people, women, and goods wherever they pass. In the west they have joined Niejiasai, and Shu troops are on the way."

sentences.zh: 」阿禮海牙益督餉西行，遣行院官塔海領兵攻帖木哥，而又設備於江、黃，置鐵繩於峽口，作舟艦以待戰。

translations.literal: Alihaiya redoubled supervision of supplies going west, sent the mobile bureau officer Tahai to lead troops against Temuge, and also made preparations on the Yangzi and Yellow rivers, set iron chains at the gorge mouths, and built warships awaiting battle.
translations.idiomatic: Alihaiya pressed supply lines westward harder, sent mobile bureau officer Tahai against Temuge, and prepared on the Yangzi and Yellow rivers—setting iron chains at the gorges and building warships for battle.

sentences.zh: 十九日，師與西兵遇於鞏縣之石渡，而湖廣所徵太原之兵最為可用。

translations.literal: On the nineteenth day the army met western troops at Shidu in Gong County; the Taiyuan troops summoned from Huguang were the most usable.
translations.idiomatic: On the nineteenth our army met the western forces at Shidu in Gong County; the Taiyuan troops summoned from Huguang proved the most reliable.

sentences.zh: 甫至，未及食，或趣之倍道以進，轉戰及暮，兩軍殺傷與墮澗谷死者相等，而虎牢遂為敵有。

translations.literal: They had just arrived and not yet eaten when some urged them to advance by double marches; fighting continued until evening, and the killed and wounded and those who fell into ravines and valleys were equal on both sides—but Hulao was thereby lost to the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: They had just arrived and had not even eaten when someone urged a forced march. Fighting lasted until evening; casualties on both sides, including men who fell into ravines, were about equal—but Hulao fell to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 兵儲巨萬，阿禮海牙盡其心、民殫其力者，一旦悉亡焉。

translations.literal: Military stores in the tens of thousands—all that Alihaiya had given his heart to and the people had exhausted their strength for—were in one day wholly lost.
translations.idiomatic: The vast stores that Alihaiya and the people had poured their hearts and strength into were lost in a single day.

sentences.zh: 行省院與諸軍斂兵退。

translations.literal: The branch secretariat, bureau, and various armies gathered their troops and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The branch secretariat, military bureau, and allied armies drew back.

sentences.zh: 二十二日至汴，民大恐。

translations.literal: On the twenty-second they reached Bian; the people were greatly terrified.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-second they reached Bian, and the populace was terrified.

sentences.zh: 阿禮海牙前後遣使告于朝，輒為也先捏留不遣，不得朝廷音問已二十日，阿禮海牙亦憂之，親出行撫其民。

translations.literal: Alihaiya repeatedly sent envoys to report to court, but they were always detained by Yexianie and not sent on; he had received no word from court for twenty days. Alihaiya was anxious as well and went out in person to reassure the people.
translations.idiomatic: Alihaiya had sent repeated reports to court, but Yexianie detained every messenger; for twenty days he heard nothing from the capital. Anxious himself, he went among the people to reassure them.

sentences.zh: 乃修城闕以備衝突，立四門以通往來，戒卒伍以嚴守衛。

translations.literal: He then repaired the city walls and towers against assault, opened the four gates to allow passage, and admonished the soldiers to guard strictly.
translations.idiomatic: He repaired the walls and towers against assault, kept the four gates open for traffic, and ordered the garrison to tighten its guard.

sentences.zh: 時雖甚危急，阿禮海牙朝夕出入，聲色不動，怡然如平時，衆賴以安。

translations.literal: Though the time was exceedingly critical, Alihaiya went in and out morning and evening without change of voice or countenance, at ease as in ordinary times, and the multitude relied on him for calm.
translations.idiomatic: Though the crisis was extreme, Alihaiya came and went morning and evening without a change in voice or expression, as calm as in peacetime, and the people took heart from him.

sentences.zh: 十一月六日，西師逼城將百里而近，阿禮海牙召行院將帥、憲司與凡在官者，而告之曰：「吾荷國厚恩，唯有一死以報上耳。

translations.literal: On the sixth day of the eleventh month, as western troops pressed the city to within a hundred li, Alihaiya summoned the mobile bureau generals, surveillance officials, and all in office and told them, "I bear the state's deep grace; I have only one death with which to repay my sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: On the sixth of the eleventh month, with western troops within a hundred li of the city, Alihaiya summoned the mobile bureau commanders, surveillance officials, and every officer on duty and said, "I owe the state a deep debt; I have only my life to repay the throne.

sentences.zh: 行院之出，唯敵是圖，而退保吾城，不亦怯乎？

translations.literal: The mobile bureau went forth with the enemy alone in view—yet to withdraw and merely defend our city, is that not cowardice?
translations.idiomatic: The mobile bureau was sent out to seek the enemy—yet we withdraw and hide behind our walls. Is that not cowardice?

sentences.zh: 然敵亦烏合之衆，何所受命而敢犯我乎？

translations.literal: Yet the enemy too are a mob gathered together—under whose command do they dare invade us?
translations.idiomatic: Yet the enemy are only a mob—whose orders do they follow that they dare attack us?

sentences.zh: 且吾甲兵非不堅勁，芻峙非不豐給，而弗利者，太平日久，將校不知兵，吏士不練習，彼所以得披猖至此。

translations.literal: Moreover, our arms and armor are not unstrong, our fodder stores not unample—what has not profited us is that peace has lasted long; officers do not know war, clerks and soldiers are unpracticed; that is why the enemy could rampage to this point.
translations.idiomatic: Our arms are strong and our fodder ample—the trouble is that after long peace our officers do not know war and our men are untrained. That is why the enemy could run wild this far.

sentences.zh: 彼誠知我聖天子之命，則衆沮而散爾，何足慮乎。

translations.literal: If they truly knew the command of our sage Son of Heaven, the host would be discouraged and scatter—what is there to fear?
translations.idiomatic: If they truly knew the command of our sage emperor, their host would lose heart and scatter. What is there to fear?

sentences.zh: 吾今遣使告于朝，請降詔大赦脅從詿誤。

translations.literal: I now send envoys to report to court and request an edict of general amnesty for those coerced and misled.
translations.idiomatic: I will send envoys to court and ask for an edict of general amnesty for those coerced and misled.

sentences.zh: 比詔下，先募士，以即位詔及朝廷招諭之文入其軍，明示利害。

translations.literal: Before the edict arrives, first recruit men to carry the accession edict and the court's proclamation of persuasion into their army and clearly show advantage and harm.
translations.idiomatic: Before the edict arrives, recruit men to carry the accession proclamation and the court's summons into their camps and make the stakes plain.

sentences.zh: 吾整大軍西嚮以征之，別遣驍將率精騎數千上龍門，繞出其後，使之進無所投，退無所歸，成擒於鞏、洛之間必矣。

translations.literal: I shall array a great army westward to campaign against them, and separately send fierce generals leading several thousand elite horsemen up Longmen to circle behind them, so that advancing they have nowhere to go and retreating nowhere to return—they will surely be captured between Gong and Luo.
translations.idiomatic: I will march a great army west to attack them and send fierce generals with several thousand elite horsemen up Longmen to take them from behind, so that advancing they have nowhere to go and retreating nowhere to flee—they will surely be taken between Gong and Luo.

sentences.zh: 而我軍所獲陝西官吏，命有司羈而食之，一無所戮。

translations.literal: As for Shaanxi officials captured by our army, order the authorities to detain and feed them, and kill not a one.
translations.idiomatic: As for Shaanxi officials we capture, order the authorities to detain and feed them, and kill none.

sentences.zh: 」衆曰：「諾，唯命。

translations.literal: The assembly said, "Yes—we obey your command."
translations.idiomatic: Everyone answered, "Yes—we await your orders."

sentences.zh: 」即日與行院整兵南薰門外以行。

translations.literal: That same day he and the mobile bureau arrayed troops outside the Nanxun Gate and set out.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he and the mobile bureau marshaled troops outside the Nanxun Gate and marched out.

sentences.zh: 會有使者自京師還，言齊王已克上都，奉天子寶璽來歸，刻日至京矣。

translations.literal: It happened that an envoy returned from the capital, reporting that the Prince of Qi had taken Shangdu and was bringing the Son of Heaven's seals back in submission, arriving at the capital on the appointed day.
translations.idiomatic: Just then an envoy returned from the capital with word that the Prince of Qi had taken Shangdu and was bringing the imperial seals home, due in the capital on the appointed day.

sentences.zh: 阿禮海牙乃置酒高會於省堂以賀，發書告屬郡，報諸江南三省，而募士得蘭住者齎書諭之。

translations.literal: Alihaiya then set out wine for a grand gathering in the secretariat hall to celebrate, sent letters to inform subordinate commanderies, reported to the three southern provinces, and recruited a man named Lanzhe to carry the proclamation to them.
translations.idiomatic: Alihaiya held a grand feast in the secretariat hall to celebrate, wrote to subordinate prefectures, notified the three southern provinces, and recruited a man named Lanzhe to carry the proclamation to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 西人猶搒掠蘭住，訊以其實，而朝廷亦遣都護月魯帖木兒從十餘人奉詔放散西軍之在虎牢者。

translations.literal: The westerners still beat and plundered Lanzhe and interrogated him for the truth; meanwhile the court also sent the protector Yelutiemuer with more than ten men bearing an edict to disband the western army at Hulao.
translations.idiomatic: The western troops still beat and robbed Lanzhe and questioned him for the truth, while the court also sent Protector Yelutiemuer with a dozen men bearing an edict to disband the western army at Hulao.

sentences.zh: 西人殺其從者之半，械都護以送諸荊王所。

translations.literal: The westerners killed half his followers and bound the protector, sending him to the Prince of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: The western troops killed half his escort, bound the protector, and sent him to the Prince of Jing.

sentences.zh: 荊王時在河南之白馬寺，以是西人雖未解散，各已駭悟。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jing was then at White Horse Temple in Henan; for this reason, though the westerners had not yet dispersed, each was already shocked into awareness.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jing was then at White Horse Temple in Henan; though the western army had not yet dispersed, each man was already shaken into doubt.

sentences.zh: 又聞行省院以兵至，猶豫不敢進。

translations.literal: Hearing again that the branch secretariat and bureau were coming with troops, they hesitated and dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that the branch secretariat and military bureau were marching against them, they hesitated and dared not advance.

sentences.zh: 朝廷又使參政馮不花親諭之，乃信服。

translations.literal: The court also sent Administrative Commissioner Fengbuhua in person to instruct them, and they thereupon submitted in faith.
translations.idiomatic: The court then sent Administrative Commissioner Fengbuhua in person to reason with them, and they submitted.

sentences.zh: 靖安王遣使四輩與蘭住來請命，逡巡而去，難平。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jing'an sent four missions of envoys with Lanzhe to request orders; they lingered and departed—the situation was hard to settle.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jing'an sent four missions with Lanzhe to seek terms; they lingered and withdrew, and peace was still hard to secure.

sentences.zh: 阿禮海牙乃解嚴報捷，斂餘財以還民，從陝西求民人之被俘掠者歸其家，凡數千人。

translations.literal: Alihaiya then lifted the alert and reported victory, gathered surplus funds to return to the people, and from Shaanxi sought commoners who had been captured and plundered to restore to their homes—in all several thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: Alihaiya then stood down the alert and reported victory, returned surplus funds to the people, and from Shaanxi recovered several thousand civilians who had been seized and sent them home.

sentences.zh: 陝西官吏被獲者，皆遣還其所。

translations.literal: Shaanxi officials who had been captured were all sent back to their places.
translations.idiomatic: Captured Shaanxi officials were all sent back to their posts.

sentences.zh: 阿禮海牙自始至鎮，迨乎告功，居汴省者數月。

translations.literal: From the time Alihaiya first arrived to govern until he reported success, he dwelt at the Bian Branch Secretariat for several months.
translations.idiomatic: From his first arrival in office until he reported victory, Alihaiya spent several months at the Henan secretariat in Bian.

sentences.zh: 後以功遷陝西行御史大夫，復拜中書省平章政事。

translations.literal: Later, for his merit he was transferred to Grand Censor of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat and again appointed Grand Councillor of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for his merit he was made Grand Censor of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat and again appointed Grand Councillor of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 奕赫抵雅爾丁

translations.literal: Yihediyaerding
translations.idiomatic: Yihediyaerding

sentences.zh: 奕赫抵雅爾丁字太初，回回氏。

translations.literal: Yihediyaerding, styled Taichu, was of the Huihui clan.
translations.idiomatic: Yihediyaerding, styled Taichu, was a Muslim.

sentences.zh: 父亦速馬因，仕至大都南北兩城兵馬都指揮使。

translations.literal: His father Yisumayin served to the post of metropolitan commander of military forces for the northern and southern cities of Dadu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yisumayin rose to metropolitan commander of military forces for the northern and southern sectors of Dadu.

sentences.zh: 奕赫抵雅爾丁幼穎悟嗜學，所讀書一過目即終身不忘。

translations.literal: Yihediyaerding from youth was quick-witted and fond of learning; whatever book he read, once seen he never forgot it for life.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood Yihediyaerding was brilliant and eager to learn; whatever he read once he remembered for life.

sentences.zh: 尤工其國字語。

translations.literal: He was especially skilled in the script and language of his country.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially skilled in his people's script and language.

sentences.zh: 初為中書掾，以年勞授江西行省員外郎，入為吏部主事，不再閱月，固辭。

translations.literal: At first he was a clerk of the Central Secretariat; for years of service he was appointed outer director of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat, entered as director of the Ministry of Personnel, and within less than a month firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a clerk in the Central Secretariat, was made outer director of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat for long service, then entered the Ministry of Personnel as director—but within a month he firmly declined the post.

sentences.zh: 擢刑部員外郎，四方所上獄，反復披閱成牘，多所平反。

translations.literal: He was promoted to outer director of the Ministry of Justice; cases submitted from the four quarters he repeatedly examined in completed dossiers, and many he reversed.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to outer director of the Ministry of Justice, repeatedly reviewed trial dossiers sent from every province, and reversed many wrongful convictions.

sentences.zh: 遷陝西漢中道肅政廉訪司僉事，不赴。

translations.literal: He was transferred to administrative aide of the Shaanxi-Hanzhong Circuit Surveillance Commission but did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to administrative aide on the Shaanxi-Hanzhong surveillance commission but did not take up the post.

sentences.zh: 改中書右司員外郎，尋陞郎中。

translations.literal: He was changed to outer director of the Right Department of the Central Secretariat and soon promoted to director.
translations.idiomatic: He was made outer director of the Right Department of the Central Secretariat and soon promoted to director.

sentences.zh: 一日，與同列共議獄，有異其說者，奕赫抵雅爾丁曰：「公等讀律，苟不能變通以適事宜，譬之醫者，雖熟於方論，而不能切脈用藥，則於疾痛奚益哉。

translations.literal: One day, discussing a case with colleagues, when someone differed from his view, Yihediyaerding said, "You gentlemen study the law; if you cannot adapt flexibly to suit the circumstances, it is like physicians who, though versed in prescriptions and theories, cannot feel the pulse and apply medicine—what good is that for the pain of illness?"
translations.idiomatic: One day, while discussing a case with colleagues, someone disagreed with him. Yihediyaerding said, "You study the law, but if you cannot adapt it to the circumstances, you are like physicians who know formulas by heart yet cannot feel the pulse or prescribe medicine—what good does that do the patient?"

sentences.zh: 」同列雖不平，識者服其為名言。

translations.literal: His colleagues were displeased, but those who understood admired it as a famous saying.
translations.idiomatic: His colleagues were displeased, but men of judgment hailed it as a memorable saying.

sentences.zh: 大德八年肆赦，廷議惟官吏因事受賕者不預。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Dade a general amnesty was proclaimed; court discussion held that only officials who had accepted bribes in the course of affairs should be excluded.
translations.idiomatic: In 1304 a general amnesty was proclaimed; the court debated excluding only officials who had taken bribes in office.

sentences.zh: 奕赫抵雅爾丁曰：「不可。

translations.literal: Yihediyaerding said, "This cannot be."
translations.idiomatic: Yihediyaerding said, "That will not do."

sentences.zh: 恩如雨露，萬物均被，贓吏固可嫉，比之盜賊則有間矣。

translations.literal: Grace is like rain and dew—all things are equally moistened. Corrupt officials may indeed be detestable, but compared with robbers and thieves there is a distinction.
translations.idiomatic: Grace is like rain and dew—it should fall on all alike. Corrupt officials are detestable, but they are not the same as robbers and thieves.

sentences.zh: 宥盜而不宥吏，何耶？」

translations.literal: To pardon robbers but not officials—why is this?"
translations.idiomatic: Why pardon thieves but not officials?"

sentences.zh: 刑部嘗有獄事，上讞既論決，已而丞相知其失，以譴右司主者。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Justice once had a prison case; the superior memorial had already pronounced judgment, but afterward the chancellor learned of the error and rebuked the chief of the Right Department.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Justice once had a case in which the superior memorial had already ruled, but the chancellor later learned of the error and rebuked the chief of the Right Department.

sentences.zh: 奕赫抵雅爾丁初未嘗署其案，因取成案閱之，竊署其名於下。

translations.literal: Yihediyaerding had never signed that dossier; he therefore took the completed case, read it, and secretly signed his name below.
translations.idiomatic: Yihediyaerding had never signed that dossier, so he took the completed file, read it through, and quietly signed his name at the bottom.

sentences.zh: 或訝之曰：「茲獄之失，公實不與，丞相方譴怒而公反追署其案，何也？

translations.literal: Someone expressed surprise and said, "In the error of this case you were not actually involved; the chancellor is just now rebuking in anger, yet you go and add your signature to the dossier—why?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked in surprise, "You had nothing to do with this case's error, and the chancellor is angry—why add your name to the file now?"

sentences.zh: 」奕赫抵雅爾丁曰：「吾偶不署此案耳，豈有與諸君同事而獨幸免哉。

translations.literal: Yihediyaerding said, "I happened not to sign this case—how could I work together with you gentlemen and alone escape blame?"
translations.idiomatic: Yihediyaerding replied, "I simply failed to sign this case—how could I work with all of you and escape blame alone?"

sentences.zh: 」丞相聞而賢之，同列因以獲免。

translations.literal: The chancellor heard of it and admired him; his colleagues were thereby spared.
translations.idiomatic: When the chancellor heard of it he admired him, and his colleagues were spared punishment.

sentences.zh: 遷左司郎中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to director of the Left Department.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director of the Left Department.

sentences.zh: 時左司闕一都事，平章梁暗都剌謂奕赫抵雅爾丁曰：「人之材幹固嘗有之，惟篤實不欺為難得，公當以所知舉。

translations.literal: At that time the Left Department lacked one director of affairs; Grand Councillor Liangandula said to Yihediyaerding, "Men's talent and ability are common enough, but steadfast honesty without deceit is hard to find—you should recommend those you know."
translations.idiomatic: The Left Department then lacked a director of affairs. Grand Councillor Liangandula told Yihediyaerding, "Talent is common enough, but steadfast honesty is rare—you should recommend men you know."

sentences.zh: 」奕赫抵雅爾丁遂以王毅、李迪為言，一時輿論莫不稱允。

translations.literal: Yihediyaerding thereupon named Wang Yi and Li Di, and public opinion at the time unanimously approved.
translations.idiomatic: Yihediyaerding named Wang Yi and Li Di, and public opinion at once approved.

sentences.zh: 又嘗論朝士，如王仁卿、賈元播、高彥敬、敬威卿、李清臣輩可大用，時諸公處下僚，後皆如其言。

translations.literal: He also once discussed court officials, saying that men such as Wang Renqing, Jia Yuanbo, Gao Yanjing, Jing Weiqing, and Li Qingchen could be greatly employed; at the time these gentlemen held lower posts, and later events proved his words.
translations.idiomatic: He also once said that men such as Wang Renqing, Jia Yuanbo, Gao Yanjing, Jing Weiqing, and Li Qingchen were fit for high office; they were then in junior posts, and later events proved him right.

sentences.zh: 遷翰林侍講學士、知制誥兼修國史，轉中奉大夫、集賢大學士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hanlin Attending Lecturer, Drafter of Imperial Edicts, and concurrent compiler of the national history, then made Grand Master for Proper Service and Grand Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Hanlin Attending Lecturer, Drafter of Imperial Edicts, and concurrent compiler of the national history, then promoted to Grand Master for Proper Service and Grand Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 未幾，除江東建康道肅政廉訪使。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed surveillance commissioner of the Jiangdong Jiankang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed surveillance commissioner of the Jiangdong Jiankang circuit.

sentences.zh: 始視事，見以獄具陳列庭下甚備，問之，乃前官創製以待有罪者。

translations.literal: When he first took office, he saw torture instruments arrayed very completely in the courtyard below and asked about them; they had been devised by a former official to await the guilty.
translations.idiomatic: On first taking office he found torture instruments laid out in full in the courtyard and asked about them; a predecessor had prepared them for the guilty.

sentences.zh: 奕赫抵雅爾丁蹙然曰：「凡逮至臬司，皆命官及有出身之吏，廉得其情，則將服罪，獄具毋庸施也。

translations.literal: Yihediyaerding frowned and said, "All who are brought to the provincial commission are commissioned officials and qualified clerks; once the facts are impartially obtained, they will confess—torture instruments need not be applied."
translations.idiomatic: Yihediyaerding frowned and said, "Everyone brought before this commission is a commissioned official or qualified clerk. Once the facts are fairly established they will confess—there is no need for torture."

sentences.zh: 」即屏去之。

translations.literal: He immediately had them removed.
translations.idiomatic: He had them removed at once.

sentences.zh: 監憲一年，贓吏削跡。

translations.literal: After one year of surveillance duty, corrupt officials vanished from sight.
translations.idiomatic: After a year in office, corrupt officials had disappeared.

sentences.zh: 至大初元，立尚書省，拜參議尚書省事，召至京師，懇辭不就。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhida the Ministry of Revenue was established; he was appointed Consultant on Ministry of Revenue Affairs, summoned to the capital, and earnestly declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Zhida reign the Ministry of Revenue was established and he was offered the post of consultant; summoned to the capital, he firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 改立中書省，復拜參議中書省事，亦以疾辭。

translations.literal: When the Central Secretariat was restored, he was again appointed Consultant on Central Secretariat Affairs and again declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: When the Central Secretariat was restored he was again offered the post of consultant and again declined on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 延祐元年卒，年四十有七。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanyou he died at the age of forty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1314 at the age of forty-seven.

sentences.zh: 脫烈海牙

translations.literal: Tuoliehaiya
translations.idiomatic: Tuoliehaiya

sentences.zh: 脫烈海牙，畏吾氏。

translations.literal: Tuoliehaiya was of the Uyghur clan.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoliehaiya was a Uyghur.

sentences.zh: 世居別失拔里之地。

translations.literal: His family had long dwelt in the land of Bieshibali.
translations.idiomatic: His family had long lived in Bieshibali.

sentences.zh: 曾祖闊華八撒朮，當太祖西征，導其主亦都護迎降。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Kuohuabasazhu, when Taizu campaigned west, guided his lord the Idiqut to welcome and submit.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Kuohuabasazhu, when Taizu marched west, guided his lord the Idiqut to submit.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其有識，欲官之，辭以不敏。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his discernment and wished to give him office, but he declined on grounds of incapacity.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his judgment and wished to give him office, but he declined as unworthy.

sentences.zh: 祖八剌朮，始徙真定，仕至帥府鎮撫。

translations.literal: His grandfather Balazhu first moved to Zhending and served to the post of pacification commissioner of the marshal's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Balazhu first settled at Zhending and rose to pacification commissioner of the marshal's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 富而樂施，或貸不償，則火其券，人稱為長者。

translations.literal: He was wealthy and delighted in giving; when loans were not repaid he burned the bonds, and people called him a man of virtue.
translations.idiomatic: He was wealthy and generous; when loans went unpaid he burned the bonds, and people called him a true elder.

sentences.zh: 父闍里赤，性純正，知讀書。

translations.literal: His father Chanlizhi was pure and upright by nature and knew how to read books.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chanlizhi was upright by nature and literate.

sentences.zh: 脫烈海牙幼嗜學，警敏絕人。

translations.literal: Tuoliehaiya from youth loved learning and was alert and quick beyond others.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Tuoliehaiya loved learning and was exceptionally quick-witted.

sentences.zh: 性整暇，雖居倉卒，未嘗見其急遽。

translations.literal: His nature was orderly and unhurried; even in sudden crises he was never seen flustered.
translations.idiomatic: He was orderly and unhurried by nature; even in sudden crises he was never seen flustered.

sentences.zh: 喜從文士游，犬馬聲色之娛，一無所好。

translations.literal: He delighted in associating with literary men and had no liking whatsoever for the pleasures of horses, dogs, music, or women.
